mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate directly lowers the risk-free rate component of equity discount rates, increasing the present value of future cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates and reduces valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates broad consumer demand contraction, triggering negative equity sentiment and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances, or interaction term Rank IC is below 0.02 over 5-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, a declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals labor market tightness that precedes inflationary pressures and monetary policy tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of late-cycle expansion periods despite declining UNRATE, or Rank IC for UNRATE decline is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates labor market strength that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS rises, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over 5-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100, it signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate output and profits, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 100, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates severe demand deterioration that triggers bearish market sentiment, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and GDPC1 fails to predict negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances, or interaction term Rank IC is below 0.02 over 5-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 5.0% YoY), persistent inflation pressures lead to aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of high inflation regime periods (CPIAUCSL > 5.0% YoY), or Rank IC for CPIAUCSL in high inflation regimes is below 0.02.
